Policy.Title: Operational policy workbench
Policy.ImmutableNotice: Job key, job type, argument contract, owner, release, worker revision, job revision, and configured timezone remain deployment-owned. Policy changes affect future admission; queued and running executions preserve their captured configuration.
Policy.MaxRecordsHelp: Leave empty to inherit 100. Set zero to disable count-based retention.
Policy.MaxDaysHelp: Leave empty to inherit no age limit.

Provenance.Help: Each row separates the immutable release default from operator intent and the behavior the scheduler will apply.

Sections.GeneralHelp: Control admission state and operator-facing job identity.
Sections.ScheduleHelp: Edit recurring cadence and boundaries in the configured deployment timezone.
Sections.ExecutionHelp: Control capacity and the retry/timeout snapshot captured by newly admitted work.
Sections.RetentionHelp: Bound terminal execution history by count and age.

Actions.ResetField: Reset this field to its declared default

Validation.DisplayNameRequired: Enter a display name within the supported length, or reset the field to inherit its declared value.
Validation.DescriptionRequired: Enter a description within the supported length, choose Clear, or inherit the declared value.
Validation.Timeout: Enter a positive timeout within the supported duration range.

Conflict.DraftsPreserved: Another operator or release changed the policy baseline ({0} → {1}). Your unsaved edits are preserved while untouched fields adopt the latest policy; review before retrying.
Conflict.ReloadFailed: The policy changed, but the latest operational baseline could not be loaded. Close and reopen the workbench before retrying.
Conflict.SameField: The latest policy changed at least one field that you also edited. Your draft wins on those fields; review the declared, override, and effective columns before retrying.
Conflict.ScheduleTypeChanged: The job changed from recurring to triggered while this Cron draft was open. The hidden draft has not been submitted. Discard only that schedule intent before saving the remaining edits.

Execution.ProspectiveNotice: Maximum concurrency governs new claims immediately without cancelling active work. Retry and timeout changes are captured only by newly admitted executions.
Execution.SubsecondPrecisionPreserved: This existing timeout includes sub-second precision. Those fractional ticks are preserved when the whole-second fields are edited.

Schedule.CronDescription: The cadence band is a prospective view of the exact Cronos runtime contract.
Schedule.CronInputHelp: A blank edited value is invalid. Use Reset to inherit the declared expression.
Schedule.CronTooLong: The Cron expression cannot exceed {0} characters.
Schedule.TimeZoneLockedHelp: Timezone is deployment configured and intentionally cannot be edited here.
Schedule.BoundaryValidationError: Complete both boundary fields and choose a valid wall time in the configured timezone.
Schedule.AmbiguousBoundary: This wall time occurs twice during daylight-saving fallback. The earlier UTC instant is used deterministically.

BoundaryFailures.Incomplete: Choose both a date and a time.
BoundaryFailures.InvalidLocalTime: This wall time does not exist because the configured timezone advances its clock.

Schedule.ValidationError: The expression is not accepted by the scheduler runtime.
Schedule.DescriptionUnavailable: A localized description is unavailable; runtime validation and preview remain authoritative.
Schedule.NonZeroSecondsConversion: This six-field expression has a non-zero seconds field. Correct it manually before switching to five fields so cadence is not silently changed.
Schedule.InvalidConversion: The current expression is invalid and cannot be converted.
Schedule.AuthoritativeObservedAt: Loaded from authoritative state observed at {0}
Schedule.PreviewSuspendedDescription: No occurrence will be scheduled while the effective policy is paused.
Schedule.ProspectiveWarning: Saving replaces the recurring cursor transactionally and schedules only the next occurrence strictly after database current time. Missed occurrences are never backfilled.

Modes.EveryDay: Every day at a selected time
Modes.EveryWeek: Every week on a selected weekday and time
Modes.EveryMonth: Every month on a selected day and time

Syntax.Title: Cronos syntax guide
Syntax.RuntimeContract: Field order is minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week; six-field mode prepends seconds.
Syntax.FieldTable: Cron field ranges and special characters
Syntax.Names: Months accept JAN–DEC and weekdays accept SUN–SAT, case-insensitively.
Syntax.ReversedRanges: Reversed ranges wrap across the field boundary, such as FRI-MON or 22-2.
Syntax.Steps: A step applies within its base range; */15 starts at the field minimum and advances by 15.
Syntax.DayMatching: When both day-of-month and day-of-week are constrained, Cronos requires both fields to match.

Tokens.Question: Any value for day-of-month or day-of-week
Tokens.Last: Last day of month or last named weekday

Examples.MonthlyFirst: At midnight on the first day of every month

Schedule.Title: Recurring schedule
Schedule.Description: The durable cursor uses this immutable schedule and the active policy to materialize occurrences.
Schedule.TriggeredDescription: This job has no recurring cursor. Operators admit an execution explicitly through the active catalog.
Schedule.DebugManualOnly: Debug mode is suppressing automatic occurrences. Run job now remains available and does not advance the recurring cursor.

StatusDescriptions.NotRecurring: No recurring cursor applies to an on-demand job.
StatusDescriptions.AwaitingSynchronization: The active declaration is waiting for the control plane to create its durable cursor.
StatusDescriptions.Scheduled: The durable cursor has a next occurrence ready for future materialization.
StatusDescriptions.Suspended: Operator policy has suspended new recurring occurrence materialization.
StatusDescriptions.Exhausted: No occurrence remains within the declared schedule boundaries.

SuspensionDescriptions.OperatorAndDebug: Operator policy and debug mode both suppress automatic occurrence materialization. Clearing the operator pause leaves debug suppression active.

Contract.Title: Declaration and policy contract
Contract.Description: Code-owned declaration fields remain immutable; operator policy is stored independently and updated with optimistic concurrency.
Contract.MaxConcurrencyHelp: Caps concurrent worker leases; recurring materialization also uses it as the queued-and-running overlap limit.
Contract.RetryCountHelp: Additional failed attempts allowed after the first attempt.
Contract.ExecutionTimeoutHelp: Maximum duration allowed for one execution attempt.
Contract.PolicyStampHelp: Optimistic-concurrency token; policy updates must match it and receive a new stamp.

LatestExecution.Title: Latest execution
LatestExecution.Description: Newest durable execution evidence for this logical job across catalog revisions.
LatestExecution.Empty: This job has not produced any durable execution yet.

Health.Title: Job health
Health.Description: Reliability, schedule delivery, terminal outcomes, and attempt duration are measured independently.
Health.ReliabilityFormulaHelp: Successful completions divided by successful plus failed completions; skipped and cancelled executions are excluded.
Health.FulfillmentFormulaHelp: Recurring schedule occurrences delivered to a worker, whether successful or failed, divided by delivered plus skipped occurrences. Triggered and operator run-now admissions are excluded.
Health.TriggeredFulfillmentNotApplicable: Triggered jobs have no automatic schedule to fulfill.
Health.OutcomeAriaLabel: Job execution outcomes created in the selected window
Health.CohortNote: Outcome tiles describe executions created in the window; reliability and duration use executions completed in the window.
